AgentExtension.description:
Agent-specific inventory attributes.

Implements MAS-AIRM §4.8 footnote 25 directly: "for AI agents, relevant attributes may include
agent-specific identifiers, information on the tools and systems the agent can access, its
components, and the guardrails imposed to manage risk". ``human_checkpoints`` serves §5.9(c)
(design for oversight, with escalation when predefined conditions are met) and
``approved_tools`` makes the §5.23(a) tool-usage monitoring checkable against approved scope.

approved_tools.description: Tools and systems the agent may access (MAS-AIRM §4.8 fn25).
approved_tools.title: Approved Tools

systems_accessible.description: Internal or external systems reachable by the agent.
systems_accessible.title: Systems Accessible

components.description: Sub-agents, planners, retrievers and other components (MAS-AIRM §4.8 fn25).
components.title: Components

human_checkpoints.description: Points at which a human must approve or can intervene (MAS-AIRM §5.9(c)).
human_checkpoints.title: Human Checkpoints

max_steps.description: Cap on autonomous steps per task, a §5.2 mitigant.
max_steps.title: Max Steps

can_initiate_external_actions.description: Whether the agent can act on systems of record or third parties (§1.11).
can_initiate_external_actions.title: Can Initiate External Actions

trace_logging.description: Reasoning, actions and tools are logged (MAS-AIRM §5.23(a) and (d)).
trace_logging.title: Trace Logging

AgentExtension.title: AgentExtension

AutonomyLevel.description:
How much the use case relies on the AI to act without a human.

Not a MAS taxonomy. It operationalises the Reliance dimension of MAS-AIRM §4.12(c) ("the
extent of autonomy granted to the AI system or model and the degree of human involvement") and
the agent risks of §1.11. Response to Feedback §7.18 contrasts automated trade execution
(higher) with staff reviewing every recommendation (lower), which is the gradient below.

``AUTONOMOUS_DECISIONING`` and ``AUTONOMOUS_AGENT`` are deliberately distinct. A real-time
fraud model that blocks a transaction without human review is fully autonomous in the §4.12(c)
sense, but it is not an AI agent: it has no tools and no systems access, so the agent
attributes of §4.8 footnote 25 do not apply to it. Conflating the two would demand agent
identifiers and tool allowlists from a scoring model, and would understate the distinct risk
§1.11 describes, where "an AI agent with access to tools could autonomously execute
unauthorised or erroneous actions".
AutonomyLevel.title: AutonomyLevel

Dependency.description:
A dependency of the use case on another system, model or dataset.

Serves MAS-AIRM §4.7 ("dependencies") and §4.10 fn26, which requires dependencies between AI
systems or models to be considered where they affect the use case's risk profile. The
``identifier`` field carries the shared key that §4.6 fn23 expects for linking the AI inventory
to data and third-party registers.

identifier.description: Shared identifier linking to another register (MAS-AIRM §4.6 fn23).
identifier.title: Identifier

affects_risk_profile.description: Whether this dependency changes the use case's risk profile (§4.10 fn26).
affects_risk_profile.title: Affects Risk Profile

Dependency.title: Dependency

Guardrail.description:
A guardrail imposed on the use case.

Serves MAS-AIRM §4.8 fn25 ("the guardrails imposed to manage risk") and §5.15, which expects
the *effectiveness* of guardrails to be tested for Generative AI and agents. ``tested`` and
``evidence_ref`` are what makes that expectation checkable.

evidence_ref.description: Evidence id or path for the effectiveness test.
evidence_ref.title: Evidence Ref

Guardrail.title: Guardrail

LifecycleStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of an AI use case.

Serves MAS-AIRM §4.7 ("lifecycle status") and §5.1 fn27, which defines the life cycle as
running from inception to retirement or decommissioning. ``pilot`` is included because the
Response to Feedback §2.9 confirms pilots and proof-of-concept deployments are in scope, and
§5.2 fn28 governs partial deployments.
LifecycleStatus.title: LifecycleStatus

ReviewStatus.description:
Model review status.

Serves MAS-AIRM §4.7 ("model review status"), §5.18-§5.21 (pre-deployment reviews) and §5.24
(re-validation). ``independent_validation`` is the formal independent validation that §5.19
expects for high-materiality use cases; ``peer_review`` is the §5.20 alternative.
ReviewStatus.title: ReviewStatus

Role.description:
A named person or function accountable for part of the use case.

Serves MAS-AIRM §4.7 ("key roles and responsibilities (e.g., owners, developers)"), §5.1
(assign roles across units) and §5.23(c) (an accountable person for monitoring).

party.description: Person, team or function holding the role.
party.title: Party

function.description: Control function or business unit, used to test independence (MAS-AIRM §5.19).
function.title: Function

Role.title: Role

ThirdPartyComponent.description:
A third-party AI component the use case relies on.

Serves MAS-AIRM §1.10 fn10 (definition of third-party AI), §4.2 fn21 (embedded AI in
third-party services) and §5.10-§5.11 (third-party AI management). ``embedded`` marks AI inside
a service not marketed as AI, which §4.2 requires to be identified at least for material
providers.

embedded.description: AI incorporated within a service not sold as AI (MAS-AIRM §4.2 fn21).
embedded.title: Embedded

material_provider.description: Whether the FI's third-party register marks this a material provider. Not inferred; see docs/INTERPRETATIONS.md I-11 (MAS-AIRM §4.2).
material_provider.title: Material Provider

fine_tuned_by_fi.description: FI modified or fine-tuned the component, engaging §5.10 fn38.
fine_tuned_by_fi.title: Fine Tuned By Fi

independent_assessment.description: An independent certification or external assessment exists (MAS-AIRM §5.11(a)); vendor self-attestations do not count (Response to Feedback §9.9).
independent_assessment.title: Independent Assessment

ThirdPartyComponent.title: ThirdPartyComponent

description:
An AI use case as recorded in the AI inventory.

Implements the attribute list of MAS-AIRM §4.7 (purpose and description, approved scope of use,
model type, data used, dependencies, lifecycle status, assigned risk materiality rating, model
review status, key roles and responsibilities, links to essential documentation), plus the
fields the rest of the toolkit needs to evaluate Section 5 controls: autonomy and human
oversight (§4.12(c), §5.9), third-party components (§5.10-§5.11), guardrails (§5.15) and the
agent extension of §4.8 fn25.

The entry is the unit of risk materiality assessment, which MAS-AIRM §4.10 and Response to
Feedback §7.5 anchor on the *use case* rather than the system or model.

id.description: Stable lowercase slug, e.g. 'credit-decision-model'. Rejected rather than normalised if it is not already a slug: silently rewriting an id would make the register file and the entry disagree, and the id is the key every other module, report anchor and evidence path uses.
id.title: Id

business_function.description: Business line or function, supporting §3.5(d) role assignment.
business_function.title: Business Function

approved_scope.description: Approved scope of use including jurisdiction (MAS-AIRM §4.7).
approved_scope.title: Approved Scope

processes_personal_data.description: Engages §5.4(f) data privacy and raises Impact (§4.12(a)).
processes_personal_data.title: Processes Personal Data

risk_materiality_rating.description: Assigned rating (MAS-AIRM §4.7); set by airm.materiality, not by hand.
risk_materiality_rating.title: Risk Materiality Rating

human_oversight.description: How human oversight is implemented (MAS-AIRM §5.9, fn37).
human_oversight.title: Human Oversight

affects_individuals.description: Whether outputs affect customers or individuals. Drives fairness and transparency relevance (MAS-AIRM §5.6-§5.8); see docs/INTERPRETATIONS.md I-7.
affects_individuals.title: Affects Individuals

contingency_plan.description: Fallback options for high-risk use cases (MAS-AIRM §5.3).
contingency_plan.title: Contingency Plan

kill_switch.description: Kill switch or override exists (MAS-AIRM §5.3 fn29, §5.23(b)).
kill_switch.title: Kill Switch

auto_updates.description: AI is designed to update automatically, engaging MAS-AIRM §5.25(c).
auto_updates.title: Auto Updates
